evidence.claim: Russia and Ukraine signed a landmark deal on 22 July 2022 to reopen Ukrainian Black Sea ports for grain exports after talks brokered by the United Nations and Turkey.
evidence.title: Ukraine, Russia sign deal to reopen grain export ports as war rages on
evidence.excerpt: Russia and Ukraine signed a landmark deal on 22 July 2022 to reopen Ukrainian Black Sea ports for grain exports after talks brokered by the United Nations and Turkey.
evidence.source_locator: search result snippet / Reuters dispatch summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting is independently corroborated by the official Istanbul ceremony and multiple mirrors.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but multilateral; Erdoğan is part of the mediation, not the sole cause of the outcome.
contrary_evidence: The deal was UN-brokered and depended on both Russia and Ukraine, so it is not a unilateral Erdoğan achievement.

evidence.claim: The trilateral memorandum addressed Türkiye's concerns, including arms exports and counterterrorism, and Türkiye agreed to support Finland and Sweden joining NATO.
evidence.title: Press conference | NATO Transcript
evidence.excerpt: The trilateral memorandum addressed Türkiye's concerns, including arms exports and counterterrorism, and Türkiye agreed to support Finland and Sweden joining NATO.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary NATO transcript with direct, dated statements from the summit press conference.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Erdoğan because he participated in the trilateral meeting and the memo was concluded with his assent.
contrary_evidence: This was a multilateral bargain, so it shows compromise rather than unilateral peacemaking.

evidence.claim: The Permanent Joint Mechanism was intended to ensure implementation of the Trilateral Memorandum, and the parties reported progress on technical cooperation and compliance.
evidence.title: Meeting of the Permanent Joint Mechanism – Türkiye, Finland and Sweden
evidence.excerpt: The Permanent Joint Mechanism was intended to ensure implementation of the Trilateral Memorandum, and the parties reported progress on technical cooperation and compliance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government readout of the trilateral mechanism with a clear implementation statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Erdoğan because Türkiye was the constraining party in the memorandum and the mechanism tracked delivery.
contrary_evidence: A mechanism can exist without proving that the underlying security bargain was fully implemented in practice.

evidence.claim: The Commission said that President Erdogan's announcement of another planned incursion was followed by episodes of military escalation, mutual bombardment, and mobilization by all parties.
evidence.title: Report of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Syrian Arab Republic
evidence.excerpt: The Commission said that President Erdogan's announcement of another planned incursion was followed by episodes of military escalation, mutual bombardment, and mobilization by all parties.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN commission report based on first-hand interviews, documents, photos, videos, and satellite imagery.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Erdoğan's public announcement and the ensuing Turkish military posture.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes a genuine Turkish threat environment from Da'esh and other armed actors.

evidence.claim: HRW said Turkey's planned incursion would be its fourth since 2016 and that previous incursions had been fraught with human rights abuses, including killings, arbitrary arrests, and massive displacement.
evidence.title: Turkey/Syria: Civilians at Risk in Northern Syria
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Turkey's planned incursion would be its fourth since 2016 and that previous incursions had been fraught with human rights abuses, including killings, arbitrary arrests, and massive displacement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed rights analysis published on the day of the warning, with explicit laws-of-war framing and concrete prior-incursion examples.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Erdoğan because the threatened incursion was his stated policy choice.
contrary_evidence: HRW is advocacy-oriented and assesses a threatened operation, not a fully executed 2022 ground invasion.

evidence.claim: HRW said Turkey repeatedly subjected northeast Syrian cities and towns to shelling, artillery, and drone attacks in 2022, and warned that the campaign aggravated humanitarian and displacement crises.
evidence.title: Northeast Syria: Turkish Strikes Exacerbate Humanitarian Crisis
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Turkey repeatedly subjected northeast Syrian cities and towns to shelling, artillery, and drone attacks in 2022, and warned that the campaign aggravated humanitarian and displacement crises.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights reporting on the 2022 strike pattern with explicit humanitarian consequences.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Erdoğan's government and military command structure.
contrary_evidence: The article is not a casualty audit and does not by itself establish a complete incident-by-incident legal finding.

evidence.claim: Turkey said its warplanes destroyed 89 targets in Syria and Iraq in retaliation for the Istanbul bomb attack, while the SDF alleged civilian deaths and damage to civilian infrastructure.
evidence.title: Turkish air strikes target Kurdish militants in Syria, Iraq after bomb attack
evidence.excerpt: Turkey said its warplanes destroyed 89 targets in Syria and Iraq in retaliation for the Istanbul bomb attack, while the SDF alleged civilian deaths and damage to civilian infrastructure.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting with direct contemporaneous government and opposing-side claims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdoğan because the operation was a Turkish national-security decision announced by his government.
contrary_evidence: Turkey said only terrorists were targeted; the SDF alleged civilian deaths and the destruction of grain silos, a power station, and a hospital.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan said Turkey's air operations were only the beginning and that a land operation would be launched when convenient, while creating a security corridor in Syria and Iraq.
evidence.title: Erdogan says Turkey will launch Syria land operation when convenient
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan said Turkey's air operations were only the beginning and that a land operation would be launched when convenient, while creating a security corridor in Syria and Iraq.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report directly attributes the statement to Erdoğan in a dated parliamentary speech context.
contrary_evidence: He also claimed to respect Syria and Iraq's territorial integrity, so the statement mixes coercion with legalistic framing.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Turkish drones targeted oil installations in northeast Syria, marking the first systematic Turkish targeting of oil fields there, while the SDF alleged civilian deaths and the Pentagon said the strikes threatened U.S. personnel.
evidence.title: Turkish strikes hit oil installations in northern Syria, sources say
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Turkish drones targeted oil installations in northeast Syria, marking the first systematic Turkish targeting of oil fields there, while the SDF alleged civilian deaths and the Pentagon said the strikes threatened U.S. personnel.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting combines local-source claims, Turkish rebuttal, and U.S. reaction in one contemporaneous article.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly relevant to Erdoğan because it describes a Turkish military campaign ordered by his government.
contrary_evidence: Turkey said oil fields were not targets and that it selected targets sensitively.

evidence.claim: Armed Syrian opposition groups supported by Turkey committed abuses including extrajudicial killings, unlawful detention, forced evacuations, looting, child soldier recruitment, and other violations, and there was no information available on prosecution of individual personnel.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Syria
evidence.excerpt: Armed Syrian opposition groups supported by Turkey committed abuses including extrajudicial killings, unlawful detention, forced evacuations, looting, child soldier recruitment, and other violations, and there was no information available on prosecution of individual personnel.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual U.S. government human-rights reporting summarizing multiple NGO and COI findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but important: the report ties the conduct to groups supported by Türkiye and, in some cases, to Turkish officials and effective control.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes that the SDF committed abuses, so responsibility is not exclusive to Türkiye's proxies.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 Turkish nuclear command-and-control or custody evidence is absent; the dossier mostly shows inherited treaty/NATO/IAEA posture plus civil-nuclear and mediation choices.
Direct forensic or documentary proof of Erdoğan's own assets, beneficial ownership, or personal enrichment in 2022 is still missing.
Independent corroboration beyond Reuters-style reporting is still thin for the media-control and family-access claims.
Audit-grade verification of project delivery and personnel effects is still thin; the package leans heavily on official program documents and self-reported completion counts.
